about: How equipment schedules are read off the drawing sheets (build step 4). Header words are compared after squashing spaces, ignoring case and a trailing full stop or colon. Patterns are regular expressions, matched ignoring case. Extend this file, never the code.
tag_header_pattern_about: A key-column header the exact list above misses ("UNIT", "AC UNIT", "PUMP NO.", "FAN NO.", "AC UNIT NO."), matched whole on the squashed upper-case header with its trailing stop taken off. A column so headed is the tag column only when most of its cells below are unit tags, none of them twice. Past the first column only a bare key (bare_tag_header_pattern) counts: a column of ASSOCIATED CONDENSING UNIT names another unit, not the row's.
not_header_lines_about: Words that start a line of a title block or a list that only looks like a key header (SHEET NO., DRAWING NO., ITEM NO.): the line never makes a sheet a schedule sheet. A table's own cell is still read when its cells below are unit tags.
description_headers_about: A column that says what each row is: when most of its cells name an air device, the schedule lists air devices (air_device_words).
quantity_headers_about: A column that counts the units a row stands for. A row whose tag is a type takes its quantity from it (header compared whole: NO. OF PORTS is not one).
notes_beside_about: How far to the right of a table (points) its notes are looked for when they are set beside it, not under it. The search stops at the next table.
notes_beside_above_about: How far above a table's top (points) a note set beside it may start: a heading that lines up with the schedule's title, which sits just above the table.
schedule_heading_about: A line of a sheet's text that heads a schedule ("EXHAUST FAN SCHEDULE", "ROOFTOP UNIT SCHEDULE (1 OF 2)"). When a schedule sheet's tables can't be read (a picture read by OCR), its units are counted from its text, each under the nearest heading above it.
type_list_titles_about: A schedule with one of these words in its title lists types of air device, silencer or fixture (passive items no controller serves), not units: a tag column whose prefix isn't in equipment.json is read as types there, never counted as units.
air_device_words_about: Words that say a schedule lists passive air devices (diffusers, registers, grilles, louvers, air outlets, silencers) by type: in its title, a line between its title and its header, a band row of its key column, or most of its description cells. Its codes (B1, SD-1, CD, LRD-A) are types, never units, whatever their prefix: B is a boiler's and SD a smoke damper's. A line between its title and its header, or a band row, says so only while no key cell is a unit tag of other equipment (EF-1, AHU-1, VAV-1: a prefix outside air_outlet_codes); its title says so whatever the key cells hold, and a key column that holds such a tag is said in a flag.
air_device_exceptions_about: A title with one of these words lists equipment a controller serves as well (LOUVER AND DAMPER SCHEDULE: motorized dampers), so the schedule is never taken for a list of air devices.
air_outlet_codes_about: Code prefixes common on air outlets (CD ceiling diffuser, RG return grille, SG supply grille, LD linear diffuser ...). A schedule whose key column holds nothing but codes with these prefixes (RG-1, CD-1, SD-1, TG-1, LD-A), of air_outlet_code_kinds different prefixes at least, is a list of air outlets when nothing else says what it lists: no air device word in its title or in a line above its header, no title that names equipment a controller serves (air_device_exceptions), and no description column (description_headers), whose words decide alone. SD is a smoke damper's prefix as well as a supply diffuser's, and SD or LD can be a detector's: one kind of code alone proves nothing, and a description column's words are always read first.
